behavior: Surface-dives and pursues fish underwater, propelled by its webbed feet. Gregarious and often rests on exposed perches with wings spread to dry; swims low in the water and commonly flies in shifting lines or V-formations.
field_marks: Dark brown-black body plumage with bronzy, scaled-looking wing coverts
Small head and long, kinked neck on a heavy, low-slung body
Long gray bill with a strongly hooked tip, orange-yellow facial skin, and a blue-green eye
Short black legs with large, fully webbed black feet
habitat: Freshwater and marine habitats, including lakes, ponds, rivers, lagoons, estuaries, and coasts; requires nearby exposed perches and trees, rocks, reefs, or ground sites for colonial nesting.
